chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Jumhur al-'Ammi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from 'Isam ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever from among our Shi'a preserves forty hadiths, God will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as a learned scholar and a jurist, and He will not punish him.

key_terms.أربعين حديثا: Forty hadiths - a specific number with deep significance in Islamic tradition; many "Forty Hadith" collections exist across Islamic scholarship
key_terms.حفظ: Hifz - to preserve, memorize, and maintain; in hadith context, encompasses memorization, understanding, and faithful transmission
key_terms.شيعتنا: Our Shi'a - the followers and partisans of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.عالما فقيها: A learned scholar and jurist - denoting comprehensive religious knowledge and legal expertise
key_terms.يوم القيامة: Day of Resurrection - the Day of Judgment when all souls will be raised

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for memorizing forty hadiths in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) declares a profound reward for the preservation of hadith: any follower of the Ahl al-Bayt who memorizes and maintains forty hadiths will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment with the status of a scholar and jurist, and will be spared divine punishment. This tradition was delivered in the context of encouraging the Shi'a community to actively learn, preserve, and transmit the teachings of the Imams during a period when their knowledge was at risk of being lost.
